page.layout: One page of text, single column; running head at top; a decorative ornament below the text; catchword-like line "ANNO-" at lower right; right margin holds no notes. Digitiser banner at bottom excluded.

main_text.p: VULPES etiam pirum comest. Mostell. 3.1. v.28. Tam facile vinces, quam pirum vulpes comest. Proverb. cui respondet illud Senecae de Claudio Caesare: Tam facile homines occidebat, quam canis extra colit.
main_text.head: ANIMI-TRANQUILLITATIS. ANIMI-DELIQUII. EXAMINATIONIS. INFIRMITATIS.
main_text.p: POL si animus est aequus tibi, satis habes, qui bene vitam colas. Aul. 2.2. v.10. Cicero de Senectute: Quid quod sapientissimus quisque animo aequissimo moritur, stultissimus inquissimo. Lucret. lib.5. Divitiae grandes homini sunt, vivere parce, aequo animo.
Ex deliquio animi sibi restituti solent lucem, qua aliquandiu visi carere, salutare. Mil. 4.8. v.34. Sed quid hoc? quaeres est? quid video? lux salve candida.
AQUA sevitiebat animi deliquio. Bacch. 2.3. v.14. Curc. 2.3. v.33. Truc. 2.4. v.15. Cist. 2.3. v.38. Mil. 4.8. v.22. Ter. And. 2.1. Reddidisti animum.

page.notes: Ornament (woodcut fleuron) below the text left out of transcription. Several Latin words in the italic passages are read with some uncertainty; the marginal text "Mil." and "Ter. And." references are as read. Catchword "ANNO-" is an ornamented line at lower right and may be a running catchword.
